sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: AI data-center electricity demand is structurally re-rating US independent power producers (VST, CEG) and solar equipment makers, decoupling their earnings from traditional utility cycles.

Indonesia's energy transition is bottlenecked by PLN's grid absorption capacity and coal-heavy baseload, making domestic renewables a lagging, policy-driven play rather than a market-led growth story.
US tax-credit clarity and falling module costs are compressing solar LCOE, accelerating utility-scale deployments that benefit vertically integrated manufacturers like FSLR and ARRY.
sectors.ai: Buy US-listed solar names (FSLR, SEDG, ARRY) on the AI-driven power demand narrative; Indonesia's renewables remain policy-bound, so overweight US pure-plays for beta, add CEG/VST for baseload exposure. Trim on any 5%+ gap-up; rotate into ID grid-equipment plays only after PLN capex clarity.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's rising middle-class disposable income continues to drive premiumization in snack and beverage categories, favoring nimble mid-caps over bulky conglomerates.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally lowering go-to-market costs for smaller FMCG brands, enabling outsized volume growth versus traditional retail.
Regulatory stability and food-security policies are creating a supportive backdrop for domestic consumer manufacturers, reducing input-cost volatility and boosting margin predictability.
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap FMCG names with confirmed volume breakouts (JELI, IATA, BACH) while avoiding large-cap laggards; the sector's mild aggregate gain masks strong rotational momentum into smaller consumer plays. Position for 2-4 week continuation as US-listed peers (+0.46%) confirm demand, but trim into any 15%+ single-day spikes to lock gains.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's logistics sector is structurally levered to the government's 2025 downstreaming push, which is accelerating mineral and commodity haulage demand for mid-cap truckers like TRUK and HATM.
E-commerce penetration in tier-2/3 cities remains under 30%, driving sustained growth for last-mile and cold-chain providers, with PURA and SOCI positioned to capture perishable-goods volume.
Fuel subsidy rationalization and toll-road expansion are compressing operating costs for large fleets, favoring scale players like UPS and SAIA over fragmented small operators in the medium term.
sectors.ai: Buy TRUK on the +20% breakout; it is the only mover with volume-backed momentum and direct exposure to Indonesia's e-commerce last-mile demand. Trim TAXI and SOCI into strength—their gains lack follow-through catalysts. Hold UPS as a defensive hedge; avoid chasing SAIA or BULL. Rebalance toward asset-light freight brokers and cold-chain operators ahead of Q3 peak-season volumes.

Trim OMRE/RANS into strength—conglomerate discounts persist. US names (GOOG, LYV) confirm global ad/event spending recovery, supporting IDX media sentiment.
